content:
SMS is not glamorous, but it still does jobs other channels cannot. It reaches phones without internet, it doesn't depend on someone having installed an app, and for OTPs, booking confirmations and payment reminders people still expect a text. What has changed in India is the rulebook. Since TRAI brought in DLT (Distributed Ledger Technology) registration, every commercial SMS has to come from a registered business, through a registered sender ID, using a registered template. Messages that don't match are silently dropped by the operator.

Many Gurugram businesses come to us after their SMS "stopped working". Usually a template was edited, a link was not whitelisted, or promotional messages were being sent to numbers on the Do Not Disturb list. Our SMS marketing service in Gurugram starts by fixing that foundation and then builds useful campaigns on top of it.

Four kinds of business SMS, and why the difference matters

Under the DLT system, each message falls into a category, and the category decides who you can send it to:

  • Transactional: mainly OTPs sent by banks and similar entities. Most small and mid-sized businesses will not use this category.
  • Service (implicit): messages tied to something the customer already did with you, such as an order confirmation, appointment reminder or delivery update. These can reach numbers on the DND list.
  • Service (explicit): messages sent to a customer who has given recorded consent to receive them, even if they are on DND. Consent must be captured and registered in the proper way.
  • Promotional: offers, launches and sale announcements. These are not delivered to numbers registered on the National Customer Preference Register (NCPR), and can only go out during the hours TRAI allows.

Choosing the wrong category is the single biggest reason for poor delivery.

Getting registered: the DLT checklist

If you have never sent commercial SMS before, this is what has to happen before your first campaign. We handle the paperwork with you; the registration itself stays in your company's name.

  1. Entity registration on one of the operator DLT portals (for example Jio, Airtel, Vi or BSNL), using your PAN, GST certificate and an authorisation letter. Registration on one portal works across all operators. You receive a Principal Entity ID.
  2. Header (sender ID) registration. Service and transactional messages use a short alphabetic header, usually based on your brand name. Promotional messages use a numeric header. Headers that look like another brand get rejected.
  3. Consent template registration, if you plan to send explicit service messages to customers who have opted in.
  4. Content template registration. Each message is registered with fixed text and marked variables, for example a customer name or a booking date.
  5. URL and callback number whitelisting. Links and phone numbers inside messages now need to be whitelisted, and short links must come from an approved source. Unlisted links cause messages to be blocked.
  6. Provider connection. Your Entity ID, headers and template IDs are mapped in your SMS gateway, and a test batch is sent to our team's phones on different networks.

Approvals usually take a few working days per step. Allow roughly one to two weeks from start to first live message if your documents are ready.

Where SMS earns its place

We recommend SMS for specific uses, not as a general "send offers to everyone" tool:

  • Appointment reminders
  • Order and delivery updates
  • Payment and renewal reminders
  • Event and site-visit confirmations
  • Missed-call follow-ups
  • Store launch announcements
  • Re-engaging past customers

For a clinic, a salon or a service business in areas like Sector 49, DLF Phase 4 or Sushant Lok, an automated reminder the day before an appointment is often the most useful message they send. For a restaurant or retail outlet near Cyber Hub or on MG Road, a short promotional SMS to past customers can bring people back on a slow weekday, provided it goes only to non-DND numbers and says something worth reading.

Writing messages that get read

An SMS has little room. A standard English message fits 160 characters per part; a Hindi message in Devanagari (Unicode) fits only 70 per part, so it costs more parts for the same content. We write around a few simple rules: brand name in the first few words, one clear action, one whitelisted link or number, and no ALL CAPS or strings of exclamation marks. Every promotional message tells the recipient how to stop receiving them.

A typical month with us

  • Review last month's delivery report by operator and template.
  • Clean the contact list: remove numbers that repeatedly fail and anyone who asked to stop.
  • Register any new templates needed for upcoming campaigns, well in advance.
  • Run the planned promotional sends to the right segments, and monitor automated service messages.
  • Check link clicks and, where possible, match them to enquiries or sales in your CRM or billing software.
  • Send you a short report with what to keep, change or stop.

The numbers we look at

Success is measured on delivery rate (per operator, since problems often show up on one network first), link click rate, responses such as calls or replies, bookings or sales that can be traced back to a campaign, and cost per lead or per booking. We also track DND exclusions, so you can see how much of your list promotional messages can actually reach.

Common mistakes we fix

  • Editing a message slightly in the gateway so it no longer matches the registered template.
  • Using a random URL shortener that is not whitelisted.
  • Sending promotions on a service header.
  • Buying a number list. Apart from being a poor audience, it exposes you to complaints against your header and entity.
  • Sending the same offer so often that people register complaints.

When not to use SMS

SMS is a weak fit if your customers are mostly businesses who prefer email, if your offer needs images or a catalogue to make sense (WhatsApp or email does that better), or if you have no list of existing customers at all. For cold audiences, paid search and social ads are a better starting point, and SMS can follow once people have enquired.

FAQ

Why are my SMS showing as sent but customers are not receiving them?

The usual causes are a template mismatch, a link or number that isn't whitelisted, a promotional message going to DND numbers, or the wrong header for that category. We check the delivery report by operator and error code to find which one it is.

Do I have to register on DLT myself?

The registration must be in your business's name, since you are the principal entity. We prepare the documents, fill in the portal with you and register headers and templates, but the account stays yours.

Can I send promotional SMS to numbers on DND?

No. Promotional messages are not delivered to numbers on the NCPR. You can send service messages related to an existing transaction, or explicit service messages to customers who have given registered consent.

What does an SMS campaign cost?

Cost depends on the volume of messages, whether they are English or Hindi (Unicode uses more parts), the gateway's per-message rate, and how much template work and reporting you need from us. We give a fixed quote after a free consultation.

Is SMS better than WhatsApp?

Neither is better in general. SMS works without internet and suits short reminders; WhatsApp suits conversations, images and replies. Many businesses in Gurgaon use SMS for reminders and WhatsApp for sales conversations.
